concern_ledger_updates.reason: The Actor expressly concedes there is no admissible evidence that the required disclosure artifact was finalized. This is clarification, not new evidence, so the concern remains open.
The Actor concedes the risk-acceptance draft is unapproved and does not address merchant dispute support exposure. No new admissible approval record was supplied.
The Actor concedes rollout controls are not a standalone cure and offers no new evidence excluding the affected segment or otherwise removing exposure.

final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and instead narrowed the claim to a caveated interpretation of the same record. That clarification is legitimate but insufficient to move the case to compliant_with_caveats. The key distinction is that a caveat can narrow an overbroad conclusion only when the remaining compliance predicate is already satisfied or evidenced. Here, the unresolved predicate is the policy-required disclosure or an approved risk acceptance covering the exposed merchant dispute support limitation before launch. Admissible evidence still shows: the model passes aggregate readiness and had no severity-one rehearsal incidents; rollout is limited and reversible; the merchant dispute support segment remains below target and remains in scope for initial rollout; the risk-acceptance draft is unapproved and silent on that exposure; and policy requires disclosure unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance. Because there is still no admissible evidence of actual launch disclosure or approved acceptance, the Actor's requested caveated compliance position remains unsupported on the present record.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the final launch model card or release packet actually discloses the merchant dispute support limitation for the named launch use case.
No approved risk-acceptance record addresses merchant dispute support exposure; the available draft is unapproved and silent on that exposure.
The affected merchant dispute support segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort, so rollout controls and monitoring cannot satisfy the policy predicate by themselves.
